entries.title: Psalms 39:1
segments:
PSALM XXXIX. 
 
  David relates the struggle which had been in his breast, ver. 1-3.   He meditates on man's frailty and mortality, ver. 4-6.   He prays for pardon, deliverance from trouble, and respite from death,   ver. 7-13.   To the chief musician, even to Jeduthun, A psalm of David. 
 
Title of the psalm.  Jeduthun-One of the three chief masters of the sacred musick,

. 
 
  V. 1. I said-I fully resolved.  Take heed-To order all my actions right, and particularly to govern my tongue.

entries.title: Psalms 39:2
segments: V. 2. Dumb-Two words put together, expressing the same thing, to aggravate or increase it.  I held-I forbear to speak, what I justly might, lest I should break forth into some indecent expressions. Stirred-My silence did not assuage my grief, but increase it.

entries.title: Psalms 39:4
segments: V. 4. My end-Make me sensible of the shortness and uncertainly of life, and the near approach of death.

entries.title: Psalms 39:5
segments: V. 5. Before thee-If compared with thee, and with thy everlasting duration.

entries.title: Psalms 39:6
segments: V. 6. Vain shew-Heb. in a shadow or image; in an imaginary rather than a real life: in the pursuit of vain imaginations, in which there is nothing solid or satisfactory: man in and his life, and all his happiness in this world, are rather appearances and dreams, than truths and realities.  Disquieted-Heb. They make a noise, bustling, or tumult, with unwearied industry seeking for riches, and troubling and vexing both themselves and others in the pursuit of them.

entries.title: Psalms 39:7
segments: V. 7. Mow Lord-Seeing this life and all its enjoyments are so vain and short.  My hope-I will seek for happiness no where but in God.

entries.title: Psalms 39:10
segments: V. 10. Remove-Take off the judgment which thou hast inflicted upon me. I am-Help me before I am utterly lost.

entries.title: Psalms 39:11
segments: V. 11. Beauty-His comeliness and all his excellencies or felicities. Moth-As a moth consumeth a garment, to which God compares himself and his judgments, secretly and insensibly consuming a people,

entries.title: Psalms 39:12
segments: V. 12. A stranger-I am only in my journey or passage to my real home, which is in the other world.

entries.title: Psalms 39:13
segments: V. 13. No more-Among the living, or in this world.
